Four months ago, when I applied to the #YC 2026 Summer School, I never imagined I'd be accepted. 🎉 The only thing that pushed me forward was a piece of wisdom I keep coming back to: "Do it first." One week later, the offer arrived. It's a genuine privilege to join a community of people who share the same passion for building, and to learn firsthand from some of the most influential voices in the AI era, including #JensenHuang , #SamAltman , #PatrickCollison , #JeffDean , #AlexandrWang , and many other remarkable founders and researchers. Check out my product beta 👉 https://lnkd.in/g9wWd4Uu Rewind to early 2026: I set out to design an AI workflow that could recommend and archive research papers every day. As researchers living through the rise of general AI, we're seeing publication volumes grow to 50x what they were just a few years ago. Top conferences like #CVPR and #NeurIPS have gone from thousands of submissions to more than 30,000. 📑 The bottleneck is no longer keeping up with the latest progress, it's filtering out the noise to surface the most insightful work. That's exactly what #Paperinder is built for. 💡 Over the past four months, #Paperinder has evolved into an agentic system with a purpose-built harness 🤖: a research-specific #Environment , paper-centric #Tools and #Skills , and an abstracted #Constitution that guides every foundation model, from open-source #Qwen to frontier models like #GPT and #Claude . We never really know how far an idea can go, and I think that's the heart of "Do it first." What began as a personal tool has grown into an agentic system for research work at large. That journey has led us to launch #LumeLab , our initiative focused on autonomous research. It stands on two legs. The first, #Paperinder , organizes information and helps structure thinking. The second, #Northstar (a name inspired by #FeifeiLi 's philosophy on life and research), is just getting started, designed to take a core idea and then design, run, and analyze experiments in a continuous loop. We believe the autonomous research agent is already on its way. With gratitude and anticipation, I look forward to meeting and connecting with everyone at the venue this July! #AIAgents #Startups #YCombinator #Research #26SummerSchool ...more

Month by month, I keep asking myself what the role of 3D will be in the coming era of scaling models. The explicit nature of 3D representation inherently limits its scaling potential, since 3D data is far scarcer than video and images. Some people claim “3D is dead.” As a researcher who has worked on 3D since my very first paper years ago, I have started to accept a real possibility: given a large enough volume of high-quality video data, a model may learn consistent spatial understanding and reasoning through implicitly learned representations, and this could turn out to be better than human-curated 3D representations such as point clouds or 3DGS. Here, I hear a reassuring voice saying, “3D never dies.” I believe explicit 3D representation remains very much alive whenever a task lacks the “Omni”-scale data needed to train a foundation model, and it stays an unavoidable path toward spatial intelligence. I’m currently working on a survey that comprehensively introduces the progress of 3D reconstruction foundation models: how to scale 3D, what the open challenges are, and how the field is already reshaping video generation, world models, autonomous driving, embodied AI, and spatial intelligence. Will coming soon and welcome discussion. ...more

🎉 Excited to share that my first-author paper, RayMap3R, has been accepted at ECCV 2026! In 3D reconstruction, RayMap is widely used to encode camera pose. We found that it carries a useful static prior💡:in streaming reconstruction models like CUT3R, feeding only the RayMap as input pushes the model to “recall” the repeatedly observed static structure while overlooking dynamic regions. 🤔 We turn this property into a signal. RayMap3R is a training-free dual-branch design that contrasts the RayMap-only branch against the full image branch. The per-pixel depth discrepancy softly localizes dynamic regions, letting us reduce dynamic interference, cut camera drift, and improve reconstruction quality. ✅ So far we have validated this on online streaming method, and we hope it can inspire stronger dynamic-scene performance in offline approaches like VGGT as well. 🙏 🌟 Project: https://lnkd.in/d89XwppV 🔗 Paper: https://lnkd.in/dBthy_WA 💻 Code: https://lnkd.in/dSVaCUBp #ECCV2026 #ComputerVision #3DReconstruction #DynamicScenes #ECCV #Spatial ...more

Happy to share our ICLR 2026 paper: CogniMap3D: Cognitive 3D Mapping and Rapid Retrieval. 🎉 A question that interests me 🤔: in dynamic 3D scenes, how can a system do more than just reconstruct what it currently sees? Can it remember a scene over time, and quickly recognize it again when revisiting, like humans do every day? In CogniMap3D, we present a cognitive mapping system that stores, recalls, and updates scene memories over time. Check the details 👉 🔗 Paper: https://lnkd.in/exUc4CJU 📄 Slides: https://lnkd.in/e2MTUwgg 💻 GitHub: https://lnkd.in/e7ZDGKgW CogniMap3D does this through three main components: ✅ Multi-stage motion cues: progressively identify dynamic regions by combining optical flow, geometry-based motion analysis, and robust keypoint refinement ✅ Cognitive mapping system: store, recall, and update static scene memory across multiple visits ✅ Factor graph optimization: refine camera trajectories with stronger geometric consistency A personal thought: recent work in 3D vision is gradually moving beyond reconstruction alone. We are starting to see more research on reconstruction + understanding and reconstruction + generation. This work is our attempt to explore how memory can also become part of 3D reconstruction systems. If you are attending ICLR 2026, our poster is at: 📍 Pavilion 4, P4-#3311 🕒 Fri, Apr 24, 2026 · 1:15 PM – 3:45 PM CDT I will not be there in person, but I’d be very happy to chat about the work — feel free to DM me. Big thanks to my co-authors and everyone who supported this work. #ICLR2026 #ComputerVision #3DVision #SceneUnderstanding #SLAM #Robotics #EmbodiedAI #VisualAI ...more

4 Agent Strategies I Discovered While Building an AI Research Platform ⚡ I've been building Paperinder, an AI-powered platform for research paper recommendation and organization. Along the way, I picked up some strategies for working with general-purpose LLMs that I think are worth sharing. I'll say "agent" to stay model-agnostic, though I primarily use Claude. Feedback welcome! 👇 1. Reflection 🔄 When an agent gives you an answer, it often covers most of the ground, but not all of it. Simply prompting the model to reflect on its own response frequently surfaces finer details, and sometimes even leads it to revise earlier conclusions. Reflection isn't just a human virtue. Models benefit from it too. Whether this stems from how uncertainty and context interact internally, the practical takeaway is clear: one pass is rarely the best pass. 2. Critics 🤝 Inside Paperinder, I built an interesting feature called "Roundtable". The primary agent, Lumeni, answers the user's question. A separate Critic agent then challenges Lumeni's response and proposes improvements. They iterate until they converge. Here's the fun part: even without setting a conversation limit, they consistently reach consensus within just a few rounds on their own. 🎯 The most entertaining discovery? When I set Claude as "Lumeni" and GPT as the "Critic", the difference in reasoning style becomes immediately obvious. It genuinely feels like a clash of two distinct cognitive frameworks. ⚔️ 3. Auto-Debug 🌙 As a solo developer, I can't manually hunt down every bug. So before going to bed, I spin up an auto-debug session where the agent simulates real user interactions, evaluates response quality, and flags issues autonomously. A nice bonus: it makes good use of CLI usage that would otherwise go idle overnight. No wasted compute. 😄 4. CLI Over Token Billing 💡 Token billing is powerful but unpredictable. An unattended agent session can quietly drain your budget. CLI-based access keeps costs within your existing subscription, and for solo developers, that peace of mind has real value. It also deploys cleanly in web-launched projects, at least those started via VS Code. 🚀 Coming soon: Paperinder is an AI-powered research assistant that grows with your research journey. It delivers daily arXiv paper recommendations tailored to you, refines your research profile based on how you rate each suggestion, and draws on a built-in RAG layer to remember your saved papers and past notes. The more you use it, the better it captures your research taste. The plan is to release it as open-source and free, with a macOS app to follow for researchers outside of CS who prefer a native experience. Drop a comment if any of this resonates, or if you have ideas to push these further! 💬 Always curious about what's next in 3D vision and beyond 🤗 For more interesting research and ideas, check out my homepage 👉 https://lnkd.in/gjmtSzt7 #AIAgents #LLMOps #AI #ResearchTools #LLM ...more

🚀 Excited to share our new work: Agentic Commerce World: An Auditable and Verifiable Environment for Vibe Commerce We introduce a new platform for vibe commerce. Similar to vibe coding, people express their commercial goals in natural language and delegate decision-making, negotiation, and transaction execution to AI agents. Vibe Commerce is fundamentally bilateral and multi-agent. Buyer and Merchant agents represent different sides of a market, pursue private objectives, and interact strategically while retaining separate authority. To support this setting, we built: 🔗 Vibe Commerce Protocol (VCP) Agents propose actions, the Commerce Intelligence Platform validates them, and the World records their actual effects. This makes agent behavior reproducible and auditable. 🌐 Agentic Commerce World (ACWorld) ACWorld is a persistent environment in which multiple Buyer and Merchant agents can interact throughout ongoing transactions. 🧠 ACWorld also generates structured interaction trajectories that can support agent evaluation and future training through process supervision, imitation learning, and reinforcement learning. 📊 We release two benchmarks: 200 tasks covering 80 commerce capabilities 60 tasks over 785,022 searchable listings Across ten models, performance ranges from 65.9% to 85.6% on the capability benchmark and from 56.1% to 91.4% on the large catalog benchmark. 🔍 Notably, some incorrect executions still reached apparently valid final states. Evaluating commercial agents, therefore, requires examining both the outcome and the process that produced it. We hope ACWorld can support research into agentic commerce, buyer-merchant interaction, agent training, and reliable execution. 📄 Paper: https://lnkd.in/dnGxDwdH 💻 Code and benchmark: https://lnkd.in/dUGvTCNF Grateful to work with Mingdai Yang , Duohao Wang, Canyu Chen , Yongfeng Zhang, Hua Wei , Manling Li , Julian McAuley , Kun Zhang, Philip Yu , Colleen(Kejing) Y. , and Zhiwei Liu . #AIAgents #AgenticCommerce #MultiAgentSystems #Benchmark #AgenticEnvironment

After an unforgettable summer at ByteDance in the Bay Area, it is time to say goodbye. Over the past three months, I had the opportunity to lead two projects focused on agent sandbox environments and agent harnesses. This experience gave me a much deeper understanding of how LLM agents can be applied to real-world problems. My biggest takeaways from this journey are: • Agents can meaningfully improve productivity and expand what people are able to accomplish. • A well-designed harness is essential for turning model capabilities into reliable applications, but the model itself ultimately determines the capability ceiling of an agent. • High-quality data remains the fundamental driver of model improvement. These lessons have made my next direction clear: I want to continue working closer to the foundation model itself and explore how we can build models that are more capable, efficient, and adaptable. With that goal in mind, I am excited to join the #AICenter at #SamsungResearchAmerica as a Research Intern this Fall, where I will focus on foundation models and efficient machine learning. I am deeply grateful to everyone at ByteDance who supported, guided, and worked alongside me throughout this journey especially my collaborators Daoan Zhang and Dehai Min . Thank you for making this summer such a meaningful and memorable chapter. With graduation now in sight (May, 2027), I am officially on the #jobmarket for full-time Research Scientist and Applied Scientist positions starting in #May #June #2027. I am particularly interested in foundation models, LLM post-training, efficient machine learning, and agentic AI. If you know of a relevant opportunity, I would greatly appreciate a referral or introduction! #FoundationModels #LLM #MachineLearning #AgenticAI #OpenToWork

It's surreal to write this post. It's been 8 years ago, when my life completely changed. All I knew about NVIDIA at the time was this magical box -- the GPU — that was producing our papers at University of Toronto. I entered the world of NVIDIA on May 6, 2018 by Jensen’s invitation. And behind the magical box, the magical universe unveiled. The universe of some of the smartest and kindest people I've ever met. People that became my dearest collaborators, colleagues, and friends. A place where a mission unites people and clears all artificial boundaries between teams. A place nurtured by a leader so unique in so many ways that it's almost hard to believe he exists. A place that became more than work, it became my home. We grew the team grounds up, with gravity in Toronto and expanding globally over the years. The mission of the team was to develop new technologies for simulation to power the creation and modeling of virtual worlds. And I couldn't be prouder of what we have achieved. Together, we've learned how to become a research lab in industry. Transitioning from conceptual work we discussed in papers, several of which won best paper awards, to technology that shipped in production and made a real world difference. NuRec, Cosmos, Alpamayo, and OmniDreams are some of the efforts I'm most proud the team has led or contributed to, and so many research works we developed through the years that have empowered them. I'd like to thank everyone for this wonderful journey, especially Jensen Huang , Rev Lebaredian , Bill Dally and Xinzhou Wu who mentored and supported me and the team through the years. But most of all I'd like to thank my team. They’ve made the NVIDIA Spatial Intelligence Lab ( https://lnkd.in/g5DamEbk ) a magical place, a frontier lab in the 3D AI domain, and a kind and collaborative environment where people care about each other and support themselves to drive impact. I couldn't be prouder of what we accomplished and the leaders they have all become. I’ve made the difficult decision to leave NVIDIA. I'm leaving with more love for NVIDIA, so much more than what I came in with. I'll miss you all dearly, and can't wait to see how you continue to change the world 💚 World models is where the next breakthrough lies, and it is around the corner. Our vision started with GameGAN in 2020, where AI reproduced a PacMan game. It was immediately clear this will be the technology to change the game for robotics. DriveGAN (2021) was our first driving simulator fully trained from data. Then came videoLDM (2023) that changed the game for video generation efficiency, Cosmos (2025) as an open world simulation platform for Physical AI, and finally OmniDreams (2026) where for the first time we demonstrated real time interactive driving in a fully AI generated world. I’m super excited for what’s to come.

Seeing research move from prototypes and papers into production was incredibly rewarding. I’m grateful to Jensen Huang , Sanja Fidler , Rev Lebaredian , Xinzhou Wu and the many others who created an environment that enables ambitious research and allows researchers to share their work through publications and open-source releases. NVIDIA has built a rare bridge between fundamental open research, large-scale engineering, and real-world impact. It is a truly special place to work, and I’m proud to have contributed to its journey in physical AI and simulation.
